# Frozen internal C++ pairing fixture

`headers.json.gz` contains the byte-for-byte tracked header closure of
`include/pineforge/engine.hpp` at commit
`38dc73e5503fe5395458e5f8df2a2ad78054a1ae`. `manifest.json` records every SHA-256
and Git blob ID, plus the compressed archive digest. The archive is UTF-8 JSON
mapping include-relative paths to exact file contents, gzip-compressed with
`mtime=0`. This keeps the fixture independent of Git history, shallow checkout
configuration, network access, and future current-header changes.

The ten headers are production source frozen only as a compilation fixture.
Do not update their financial behavior or use them to execute strategies.
`pineforge/version.h` is generated by CMake and comes from the test's
`--generated-include`; the frozen headers do not use its version macros in
class layout or entry signatures. Every other project header dependency is
frozen in the archive.

`scripts/check_script_cpp_abi.py` verifies all digests before compiling native
and generated-style callers against this exact `engine_script_run_v2` header.
Each caller must first compile successfully. Current callers must link the
current v3 runtime; frozen callers must fail that link on a missing v2 engine
entry symbol. A second fixture defines only the frozen v2 entry symbols to
prove the frozen callers can link and current v3 callers cannot. That reverse
control is not a full historical runtime. The original unversioned negative
control is retained. No linked executable is run.

The protection applies to the internal C++ header/object/runtime pairing.
It does not authenticate an erased C handle from an unrelated loaded module,
nor reject an entirely old self-contained module through its unchanged public
C ABI. Host provenance and matched module/runtime ownership remain required.
